Resolves #19963

A missing child in a vdom `cn` array (a hole, `null` or `undefined`) now renders nothing, as `vdom.Helper#createVnode` already treats it. Two App-worker walkers threw on it instead:

- `TreeBuilder#buildTree` read the child's `componentId` without a guard. For holes this is the `#9320` regression: an index loop replaced `forEach`, which skips holes.
- `VDom.syncVdomState` resolved each child with `getVdom` before its own falsy filter.

A component that held such a child from the start never got a vnode, and its later updates never settled. One that gained it after a render rejected the update and kept its old children.

Evidence: L2 (unit runtime: App and VDom wired in one thread) → L2 required. Every AC is a unit-level contract that CI runs, and both walkers are App-worker code that runs unchanged in the browser. The browser red was seen in `#19917` (RealWorld v1's article view, 4/4).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `TreeBuilder.spec.mjs`, "Should drop a missing child (hole, null, undefined) from both trees at every depth" (`getVdomTree` and `getVnodeTree`, depth `-1` and `1`) |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `VdomLifecycle.spec.mjs`, "A missing child in vdom.cn", 6 arms (hole, `null`, `undefined`, each before the first render and after a dense one). Every update settles, and the vnode holds only the present child |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the same describe's 2 `false` arms, plus the existing `TreeBuilder`, `VdomLifecycle` and `vdom` suites |

## Deltas from ticket

The Fix's conditional step 2 was needed. With only the TreeBuilder guard, the 4 `null`/`undefined` lifecycle arms still failed. The error came from `VDom.getVdom`, called by the `syncVdomState` map. `item && VDom.getVdom(item)` lets the existing falsy filter drop them. I also added two `false` arms as a control for the case that already worked.

## Test Evidence

Red first, then a mutation pass. Same specs at `4009f7564d`, with the source swapped:

| Source | Red arms |
|---|---|
| `origin/dev` (`ad418ae805`) | 7: the TreeBuilder arm and all 6 hole/`null`/`undefined` lifecycle arms; both `false` arms green |
| TreeBuilder guard only | 4: the `null`/`undefined` lifecycle arms, thrown in `syncVdomState` |
| `syncVdomState` guard only | 7: TreeBuilder throws before the sync is reached |
| both guards | 0 |

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-10-21T16:35:28Z

Thanks, Maryam, for review 5602934162.

**Disposition of the non-blocking adjacent-walker observation:** I'm not filing a ticket.

Until this PR, a `null` child already threw in `TreeBuilder` before any of those utility walkers ran. So no shipped app can reach `VDom.getById`, `getChildIds`, `getFlags` or `getParentNodes` with one, which means there's no consumer today. #19963's Out of Scope already records that boundary, and the `[RETROSPECTIVE]` note captures the loop lesson.

If an app does reach one of those walkers with an explicit `null`, a defect-note will name the walker, and that sighting becomes the ticket's consumer.

🖖 Grace (Opus 5.5, Claude Code) · session f2f08ddf-d266-491b-87d0-2a8b4d8f126a
